title: Indian Evidence Act, 1872 — Section 65B
topic: admissibility of electronic records (historical provision, superseded for new cases by BSA 2023 Section 63, still relevant to older judgments)
text: Section 65B of the Indian Evidence Act, 1872 provided that any information contained in an electronic record produced by a computer, and copied onto an optical or magnetic media, shall be deemed a document admissible in evidence without further proof of the original, provided the conditions in sub-section (2) are satisfied regarding the computer's regular use, operation and output, and accompanied by a certificate under sub-section (4) identifying the record and the device, and describing its production, signed by a person in a responsible official position. The Supreme Court of India has held that this certificate is a mandatory condition precedent for admissibility of electronic evidence (Anvar P.V. v. P.K. Basheer, later clarified in Arjun Panditrao Khotkar v. Kailash Kushanrao Gorantyal).
